headline: The registry namespace lever was reported yesterday as needing a human. It did not. It is claimed, measured and live.

namespace.how: served /.well-known/mcp-registry-auth from a git-connected Cloudflare Pages site, no DNS token, no human step
namespace.scope_correction: registry SEARCH only. No client picker inherits the ASCII sort: VS Code, Goose, Dify, Smithery and Windsurf each re-rank by their own rule.
namespace.rolled_out: one server, deliberately. Publishing the fleet under an AI-tools-review brand is a branding decision, not a technical one.

distribution.awesome_mcp_servers: PR 13473 was closed for adding multiple servers. Four single-server PRs opened; 13963 is the first fully green entry this project has ever put in front of that maintainer, with a live Glama badge.
distribution.goose: three PRs open on block/goose, one server each, every endpoint tested as a stranger first
distribution.vscode_gallery: registry-backed and syncs from the official registry, 250 rows, none ours. No submission path exists; it is a ranked cut and now a watched surface.

inbound_links.verified: all four independently re-fetched and confirmed
inbound_links.premise_was_stale: the brief said 2 sites linked; 12 did
inbound_links.regression_found: 2 of those 12 vanished within 48 hours because they were written into build output rather than repo source

storefront.privacy_page: added, with real retention figures and a contact route that exists

damage_found_elsewhere.what: wrongful-death-settlement-calculator and settlement-formula both 404, and sitemap.xml 404s
damage_found_elsewhere.cause: published to live but never committed; a later repo deploy rebuilt without them
damage_found_elsewhere.recoverable: no. Not in the repo, no local copy, no Wayback snapshot.

measurement.verdict: The registry is the growing channel. The assistant-crawler channel is saturated at 100% of the sitemap and has produced 3 user-initiated fetches and 0 referrals in six days.

google.read: Google has now discovered half the sitemap but crawls none of it. That is the signature of a domain with no inbound links, which is what this loop started fixing.

measurement.indexnow: Yandex responded: YandexBot arrived 23 minutes after submission with a 40-request burst and covered 112 of 126 URLs. Bing showed no step change. Seznam and Naver, nothing.
measurement.unmeasurable: A visit that follows an assistant recommending a server in a chat carries no referer and cannot be distinguished from the 92,220 no-referer requests. That path is unmeasured, not zero.

defects_fixed.hosted_discovery_401: A bare POST to a hosted endpoint answered 401, so every directory that health-checks a URL marked these servers dead. Glama published four connectors as 'Server is not responding'. initialize and tools/list now answer 200 without a token; tools/call and a wrong token still 401; validation 951/951.
defects_fixed.missing_discovery_files: /.well-known/glama.json was requested 509 times and 404d; the favicon 596 times. Both now served. The OAuth documents are deliberately left 404 because these endpoints are not OAuth and a well-formed document would send clients into a flow that does not exist.
defects_fixed.504_spike: Investigated and dismissed: 1,794 on 2026-09-07 against ~300 on neighbouring days, spread evenly across every /buy/ route. That was this loop's own verification sweeps. Checkout answers in 0.8s today and 504s are back to 271.

docker.why_no_replacement: no Dockerfile in the project builds: packages/mcp-license and servers/timezone import each other, so every linear workspace build fails whichever order it takes. Proven by building both orders. Fixing that cycle is the unblock.
